docs.title: Capability and Ownership Matrix
docs.text: The Capability and Ownership Matrix is a planning tool for comparing capability maturity, ownership, dependencies, and planned evolution across audiences and domains.

docs.title: The three views
docs.text:
View Use it to Matrix Compare capability maturity across audience perspectives. Capability journey Inspect current and target maturity, dependencies, and ownership for one capability. Federated domain map Explore capability relationships and appliance/federated boundaries.

The selected capability, audience perspective, and current/future state remain shared as you navigate between views.

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A["Capability YAML"] --> B["React app"]
    B --> C["Matrix, journey, and domain map"]
    B --> D["Python sidecar"]
    D --> E["Draft manifests"]
    B --> F["Tauri app data"]
    B --> G["Export YAML"]

The app's bundled sample is src/data/capabilities.yaml. Its content is illustrative. Read the user guide to configure a project and use the import/export workflow, or the YAML format reference to prepare a file.

Content integration status

The DITA panel records proposed mappings only. It does not validate a Heretto configuration or publish embedded content or PDF manuals.

docs.title: Start the application
docs.text:
For the browser preview, install the JavaScript dependencies and start Vite:

npm install
npm run dev

Browser edits are held in memory; export the YAML to keep them.

For the Tauri desktop app, create the project virtual environment and build the Python sidecar:

python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
npm install
npm run sidecar:build
npm run tauri dev

The sidecar build uses this .venv. It creates a platform-specific executable in src-tauri/binaries/; build it on each target operating system and architecture before packaging.

docs.title: Configure a project
docs.text:
The current app has no separate project-settings screen. Configure a project by preparing its capability YAML file, then importing it in the app. Start from the bundled example at src/data/capabilities.yaml, save a project-specific copy, and edit its capabilities records. See the YAML format reference for required fields and validation rules.

Each capability should have a unique, stable id; dependencies refer to those IDs. Record the current and future owner, maturity values, and audience-specific DITA planning metadata as applicable. The sample's values are placeholders, not project defaults or validated content mappings.

docs.title: Import YAML
docs.text:
1. Select Import YAML in the app.
  2. Choose a .yaml or .yml file with a nonempty capabilities list.
  3. The app parses and validates the data, then replaces the active capability set if validation succeeds.
  4. The first imported capability becomes selected. Choose the capability, perspective, and current/future state using the controls.

If parsing or basic record checks fail, the app reports an error and retains the current capability set. The desktop sidecar also checks owner values and dependency references. The browser preview does not run the sidecar, so check those fields yourself before importing there.

In the desktop app, a successful import also saves the YAML in the Tauri application data directory as capabilities.yaml. In the browser preview, the import only updates the current session.

docs.title: Edit and export
docs.text:
Choose Edit capability to update the selected record. Saving validates the full set, including dependencies, and updates the record in all three views. Desktop edits are saved to the app data file; browser edits remain in memory.

Choose Export YAML to download the current capability set as capability-ownership.yaml. Export before closing the browser preview if you want to keep your changes. Export is also useful for creating a portable project backup or sharing it with another user.

docs.title: Navigate and print
docs.text:
• Choose Matrix, Capability journey, or Domain map in the sidebar.
  • Choose a capability and audience perspective in the header.
  • Switch between Current and Future to compare the current record with its target maturity and future ownership.
  • Select Print report to print the active view.
  • Select Content mapping to inspect proposed DITA metadata. This is planning information only, not a validated Heretto configuration.

docs.title: Build the documentation
docs.text:
The Markdown source lives in site/. With the project virtual environment active, preview changes locally or write the static HTML to docs/:

.venv/bin/mkdocs serve
.venv/bin/mkdocs build

Mermaid diagrams are rendered with Mermaid.js in the Material theme.

docs.title: YAML format
docs.text:
YAML is the canonical capability document. The app accepts a top-level object containing a nonempty capabilities array. It also supports a bare array of capability records. Exported files use the versioned object shape:

version: 1
capabilities:
  - id: contextual-guidance
    name: Contextual guidance
    current: 3
    target: 5
    owner: appliance
    futureOwner: federated
    summary: Guidance at the point of need.
    decision: Define the ownership handoff.
    dependencies:
      - content-service
    dita:
      audience:
        - client
        - consultant
      maturity: phase-3
      ownership: appliance-native

See the full bundled sample for additional records and dependencies.

docs.title: Capability fields
docs.text:
Field Required Meaning id Yes Unique, nonempty identifier. Other capabilities use it for dependencies. Keep it stable when renaming a capability. name Yes Nonempty display name. current Yes Nonnegative numeric current maturity. target Yes Nonnegative numeric target maturity. It must be at least current. owner Yes Current owner: appliance or federated. futureOwner Yes Planned owner: appliance or federated. summary No Short description for the capability. decision No Scope, ownership, or planning decision. dependencies No List of other capability IDs. Use [] when there are none. dita No Proposed content metadata; fields are planning values only.

Maturity is nonnegative and can extend beyond 8 for a wider-domain horizon. The current validator does not impose a maximum. Audience identifiers used by the app are client, consultant, product-team, leadership, and wider-domain.

The optional dita object can contain:

Field Example Purpose audience [client, consultant] Intended audience identifiers. maturity phase-3 Proposed maturity tag. ownership appliance-native Proposed ownership tag.

docs.title: Validation rules
docs.text:
• The capability list must contain at least one record.
  • Each record must be an object with a unique, nonempty id and a nonempty name.
  • current and target must be numeric and nonnegative; target must not be lower than current.
  • owner and futureOwner must each be appliance or federated.
  • dependencies must be a list of IDs that exist in the same file. A capability cannot depend on itself.

The app checks basic record structure and numeric fields. In the desktop app, the Python sidecar additionally checks owner values and dependency references. The browser preview does not run the sidecar: it does not verify dependency IDs, and unrecognized or missing owner values default to appliance. For consistent results, provide every field shown in the example and use the values in this reference rather than relying on importer defaults.
